chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadeed from Jamil ibn Darradj from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:
"A man does not inherit if he kills his son or his parent, but the inheritance belongs to the relatives of the killer."
ai.seo_question: Does a killer inherit from the person they killed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific application of 'blocking by homicide' (man'u bil-qatl) to direct lineal relationships, distinguishing it from broader interpretations. It establishes that the killer is entirely excluded from the estate, which is then distributed among the remaining heirs of the deceased, reflecting the juristic principle that homicide severs the right of inheritance. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the precise distribution of wealth when a direct ancestor or child commits murder.
